pages.speaker: tomas
lines: There you are. I thought I'd have to come and fetch you.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You said you wanted me to look at the lanterns.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I do. At the school. Liam's mother asked if we could help
this afternoon.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Both of us?

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: She said another pair of hands would be welcome. I told
her you'd probably come.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Probably?

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: (a little sheepishly) I hadn't asked you yet.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You could have started with that.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Will you come?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes. Let me check with Serene first.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: I heard you. Go along. I have that request to write, and
the children will be glad of the help.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Are you sure you don't need anything?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: A little quiet, perhaps.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Come on. We can manage that somewhere else.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: (amused) Thank you, Tomas.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: All right. Let's see what they're making.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Liam's mother is getting the school ready for tomorrow's
festival. Come with me when you're ready.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Back to the fitting?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: It hasn't learned to finish itself.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: There you are! I was beginning to wonder whether I'd
have to come and borrow you myself.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Sorry. The visit ran on a little.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: I heard. You're here now. Come in, both of you.

pages.speaker: finn
lines: Can we light them yet?

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Tomorrow evening, Finn. We need to finish making them
first.

pages.speaker: finn
lines: Mine's nearly finished.

pages.speaker: tessa
lines: You haven't put the bottom in.

pages.speaker: finn
lines: Oh.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Tessa, would you show him which piece it is? Thank you.

pages.speaker: ada
lines: I've got some on my sleeve.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: The paste? Let it dry, love. It'll come off more easily.

pages.speaker: ada
lines: But now it's stuck to the paper.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Here. Keep your arm still. I'll hold the other end.

pages.speaker: pippa
lines: Is there any blue left?

pages.speaker: rowan
lines: I'm using that.

pages.speaker: pippa
lines: All of it?

pages.speaker: rowan
lines: Only this bit. You can have the rest.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Thank you, Rowan. Caelan, Liam's at the preparation
table. He's been waiting to show someone his drawing.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mum, I wanted to show Mira.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: You can show Caelan first. Mira will still get to see it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: May I?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. But I haven't finished the top.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: That's quite a roof.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's a tower.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I thought those were stairs.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: They are. That's how you get to the top.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Have you built this one with your blocks?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: A smaller one. Daisy knocked it down.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Was she helping?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: No. She wanted the piece at the bottom.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: This one's going to have a handle. So she can't reach it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: How big are you imagining it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: This big.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Something you can carry all evening, remember.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I can carry lots of things.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: I know. I'd like to see you carrying this one yourself
tomorrow.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I am carrying it myself.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You didn't carry one last year?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mum let me hold hers for a bit. But this one will be mine.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: He usually wants to get straight to the food and games.
This year he asked to make his own.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I still want to go to the games.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: So do I.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Did yours look like this when you were little?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Mine was square.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Most lanterns are square.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: He asked about mine.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mine can be a tower, though?

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Let's ask Mira what we can make from those frame
pieces she offered us.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Would you two take him over to the workshop? Mira said
she could help with a frame.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Of course. Are you expecting him back here?

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Come and find me afterward. I'll be here putting things
away, or at home once we're finished.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: If you stop to see the other preparations, stay together.
Don't go out of the village.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We will.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can I take my drawing?

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: That's what you made it for. Let this corner dry first.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I'll lift it from this side—

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Wait. I was doing that.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: (drawing his hand back) All right. Tell me when you want
a hand.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I can get it.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Mira will want to hear your idea from you, too. Give her
time to finish what she's doing.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I know.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Have a good time, love.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I will. Come on!

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We're coming. The three of us go together.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Take your time, Liam. Tell me if you'd like a hand.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I will.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Hello, you three. Is that the drawing I've been hearing
about?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's a tower lantern.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Come and show me. There's room on this side.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We almost added a second tower on the way here.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Did you? Let me see the first one before you put me out
of business.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: That's next year.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Ah. Plenty of warning, then.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: His mother said you had some pieces we could use.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: I put the light strips aside. The short ends should do for
the roof.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: So it can have a roof?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Let's have a look. Where does the light go?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Inside. Here.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: And where would the heat go?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Out the door.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: (laughing) He's got you there.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Then we'd better give it a chimney.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: A real one?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: An opening at the top. We can keep that pointed shape
around it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can we keep the stairs?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: We could draw them on the paper. Wooden stairs would
make it heavier.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I'll draw them round this side. So you can see them.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: That should work. Now, shall we try the frame?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: These strips will bend a little. They won't stand up on
their own until we join them.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Do I hold this one?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Yes, near the middle. Caelan, can you steady the
opposite side?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Here?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: A little lower. There.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: The roof's pulling it to one side.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I haven't let go.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: I know. The top piece is longer on this side. See where
it sticks out?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can you cut that bit off?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: I can. Or we could make the other side longer.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Then it'd be too big.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: I think you're right. I'll trim it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Does that mean it won't be a tower?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Look at your drawing. Which part makes it a tower to
you?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: The tall bit. And the point on top.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Those can stay. We just need both sides to match.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: (relieved) All right.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: We'll tie these corners first. The paper comes later.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: There's still enough room at the top for a handle.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Good. Leave the tie loose there until we've checked
where it hangs.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can I do a knot?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Of course. This corner. Keep hold of it while you pull.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's moving.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Would you like me to steady it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Just that bit.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Just this bit.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Try pulling both ends together.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Like this?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: That's it. I'll check each join before we lift it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: And then I can carry it?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Then we can see how it feels in your hand.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Ready to try? Keep your other hand underneath at first.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I'm ready.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: There's room beside you. I'll stand back.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's tipping!

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Set it down gently. You've got it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Did I break it?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: No. The handle's a little off the middle. The frame's all
right.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We left that tie loose. We can move it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: This way?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: A little. We'll try it there.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Will you hold the bottom while I lift it?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes. Tell me when to let go.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Now. Slowly.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's staying!

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Try turning a little.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Like this?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Gently. Yes, that's much better.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It looks like my drawing.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: It does.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Except the stairs.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: You haven't drawn them on yet.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Oh. Can we put the paper on now?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: First I need to secure that handle. Then we can fit the
paper without it moving around.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: You won't change where it goes?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: No. We found the right place together.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: (pleased) I did that knot.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: You did. It held when you lifted it, too.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can you leave it where I can see it?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Right here on the table. I'll be careful with it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Would you like to keep the drawing beside it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. So you know where the stairs go.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: I won't forget the stairs.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: You're leaving the point on, aren't you?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: The point stays. I'm fastening the handle, remember?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I know. I was checking.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: (amused) You've checked twice.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: And he can check again when he comes back. I'll leave
the drawing beside it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Do we have to wait here?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: You don't have to stand here watching me. I'll be getting
on with my work, too.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: What else is everyone making?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Halden's busy with the festival flour. We could go past
the mill.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can we see the wheel?

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: It's turning again. You'll see it from the path.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Stay on that path. Ask Halden where it's safe to stand.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I will.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: And we stay together, like your mum asked.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can I look at the frame once more?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Of course. There it is. I'll take care of it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. See you later!

pages.speaker: mira
lines: See you, all three of you.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: The frame and your drawing are safe here. I'll secure the
handle before we fit the paper.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We're together. Take your time, Liam.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: There you are again, Caelan. And you've brought an
audience.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Only a small one. Is this a bad time?

pages.speaker: halden
lines: You'll be out of my way there. Liam, keep this side of me.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Is it all right if I watch?

pages.speaker: halden
lines: From there, yes. You can see the wheel well enough.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Does it grind everything?

pages.speaker: halden
lines: Grain. What were you planning to put in it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Nothing.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: The wheel turns the machinery inside. The grain goes
between the stones.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: So the water doesn't go in the flour?

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: No, it turns the wheel, and then the shaft—

pages.speaker: halden
lines: You've answered him, Tomas. Let him look for a moment.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Oh. Right.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's bigger up close.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: And stronger than it looks. That's why you keep to the
path.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mira said that.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: Then she's saved me repeating myself.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You've had a busy afternoon.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: A useful one, at least. Better than standing here looking
at a wheel that won't move.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I'm glad it's working.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: So am I, lad. So am I.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Is all that flour for tomorrow?

pages.speaker: halden
lines: A fair bit of it. Bread first, then whatever else people
have promised to bake.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Buns?

pages.speaker: halden
lines: I supply the flour. You'll have to ask the people doing the
baking.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: He knows which table he's going to first.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mum said I have to eat something else before the sweet
things.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: She may have noticed what you chose last time.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: There was bread in it.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: (chuckling) Best take that argument to your mother.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Who gets the bread you make?

pages.speaker: halden
lines: The bakers make it. But at the shared tables, whoever
comes can have some.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Even if they didn't bring anything?

pages.speaker: halden
lines: Yes. Someone brings bread, someone brings a pot of
something. Someone puts out the benches.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: And some people have their hands full at home.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: There'll be loaves to send round to people who can't
come, too.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Do they still get the nice kind?

pages.speaker: halden
lines: (glancing at him) What kind were you planning to leave
them?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I didn't mean— I just wondered.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: I know. Yes, they get good bread.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I can help with the benches tomorrow.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You offered Serene already.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I haven't forgotten.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: Good. Leave the sacks to the people with carts. You've
done enough moving them for me today.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We'll let you get on. Thank you for letting us stop.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: Off you go. And Liam—ask before you go near any
machinery.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I did ask.

pages.speaker: halden
lines: You did. Keep doing it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Does Halden have to carry all those sacks?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: He has people to help. Tomas and I moved some for him
earlier.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I was glad when we finished.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Were they heavy?

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Very.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I'll help with something smaller.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You've been helping with your lantern already.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: Caelan! Come in. There's room if you don't all stand in
the doorway.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We were looking at the preparations. Would a short visit
be welcome?

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: A short one, yes. It's good to have something else to talk
about.

pages.speaker: venn_father
lines: And something else to do. I've had enough of waiting
beside that road.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: You got the cart back.

pages.speaker: venn_father
lines: I did. It's been useful already. I'm glad that business is
settled.

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: Liam, come and look.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: What are you making?

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: Something to hang up. I picked those colors.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I'm making a lantern. It's a tower.

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: Where is it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mira's got it. The handle tipped at first, but we moved it.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Liam helped tie the frame.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: And there's going to be stairs on the paper. All the way
round, I think.

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: Can you show me when it's finished?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. What are the colors for?

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: Mum's tying the pieces together. That one goes next.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: This one?

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: No, the yellow. Then the blue.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: You can finish choosing this part. Then you're resting.

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: I am resting.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: (gently) You know what I mean.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Do you want both yellow ones together?

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: One here. One at the other end.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: All right. I'll keep them there while I tie this.

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: Can I do that bit?

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: Let me manage the ties today. You tell me where each
piece goes.

pages.speaker: venn_father
lines: It'll look well over the window. We can see it from here.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Are you putting it up here, then?

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: Can I carry it to the festival?

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: We'll see how you feel tomorrow.

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: You said that already.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: I know, love. I still can't promise.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: If you stay here, would you want someone to bring food
over?

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: That would be welcome. I'll speak to Serene when we
know.

pages.speaker: venn_father
lines: We can hear some of the singing from the path. If it's a
quiet evening, we might sit by the open door.

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: I want to see the lights.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: I know. We'll do what we can.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I can still show you the tower.

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: With the stairs?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: If I can make them fit.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: There's quite a lot of stairs in the drawing.

pages.speaker: venn_child
lines: (a small laugh) I want to see it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We'll give you some quiet now. Thank you for letting us
visit.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
lines: Thank you for coming. You three enjoy your afternoon.

pages.speaker: venn_father
lines: Elira will be getting her lantern ready, if you're going that
way.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can we see hers?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We can ask. She may like some company.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: You've brought company, Caelan. Come in.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Hello, Elira. We were hoping we wouldn't interrupt.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Only my thoughts. They can wait a little.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Liam's been showing us how to build a tower.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mira helped.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Did she? What sort of tower?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: A lantern one. You can carry it, and it's got a point on
top.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: And where are you keeping this tower?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: At the workshop. Mira's making sure the handle stays
where we put it.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: A sensible place to leave it, then.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I wanted it higher, but it'd be too heavy.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We talked about that for a while.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's still tall.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: You'll have to show me when the paper's on. I should like
to see it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I will. Is that yours?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: It is. Caelan brought it down for me earlier.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Have you had it a long time?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: A good while. It needs a little looking after.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Is the handle loose?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Not this one. I've checked it, too.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: (smiling) Liam understands about handles now.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mine's in the right place. Mira said.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Then we'll both be able to carry them tomorrow.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Are you making a new one as well?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: No. This is the one I want to take.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: The one for your husband.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Yes.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Did he make it?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: He helped me mend it. He liked telling me how he would
have done it.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Was he right?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Sometimes. I tried not to make too much of those
occasions.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You said he came to hear you sing.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: That was his excuse.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Did he sing too?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Unfortunately.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: (laughing) That bad?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: He got the last line wrong every year.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: On purpose?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Some years I wondered.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Did you tell him?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Of course I told him. He said he knew the words
perfectly well.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: And then he sang it wrong again?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Louder. As though I might have misheard him.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: What did he say instead?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: He put a garden gate in it once. I asked him which song
he thought we were singing.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: What did he say?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: (laughing) That he couldn't remember the words with me
interrupting.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Did anyone else notice?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Everyone standing near us. Some of them began waiting
to hear what he'd do.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Was he cross?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: He pretended to be. He always joined in again.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I wish I'd heard it.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: (her voice softening) Yes. So do I.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Did I say something wrong?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: No, love.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: You went quiet.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: I was remembering him.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: But you were laughing.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: I was. It was funny.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: And it made you sad?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: A little. I'd have liked to hear him get it wrong again.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Would you like us to stay a little?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: I would. Thank you.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We aren't in a hurry.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: That's a pleasant thing to hear from you, Tomas.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: (a little embarrassed) I'm not always in a hurry.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: No. Not always.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: How did your mother get on with all that paper, Liam?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Ada got her sleeve stuck to some.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I held the paper while she tried to get it off.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mum said we should let it dry.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: (smiling) Was Ada willing to wait?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: She kept looking at it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Your mum had us helping before we'd got through the
door.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Good for her.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Are you still going to sing tomorrow?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Yes. I mean to.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Will people sing with you?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Some will. Some would rather listen.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We'll come and find you.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: I'd like that. Liam, bring your tower where I can see it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. I'll show you the stairs as well.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I could carry your lantern down for you tomorrow.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Thank you. I'd like to carry this one myself.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: All right.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: You can mind the door when I bring it out. It catches
when I've got both hands full.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I can do that.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Then we'll see you tomorrow. Will you be all right here?

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Yes, Caelan. Thank you for the company.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Thank you for showing me your lantern.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: You're welcome, love. I'm glad you asked.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mira hasn't put the paper on mine yet.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: There's still time today. Let her finish the part she's
doing.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We'll leave you to get ready.

pages.speaker: elira
lines: Go on, then. And don't let that tower get away from you.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I'll keep hold of it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Will Elira really sing tomorrow?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: She said she would.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Even if it makes her miss him?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes. I think she wants to.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We can go and listen.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I want to show her the tower.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We will. Let's give her some quiet now.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Caelan?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can we go home for a little while?

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Tired?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: My feet are. And I'm hungry.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Of course. We've been walking quite a bit.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Your frame's still at Mira's.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I haven't forgotten it.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I didn't think you had.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We can collect it on the way. If the handle's ready, you
can take it home.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: And the drawing.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: And the drawing.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I want to try the stairs before Mum sees it.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We can look at them after you've had something to eat.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. Come on.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: There's no hurry. We'll walk.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: The handle's secured. Your frame and drawing are here
when you're ready, Liam.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Back already? How did you get on?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: We saw Elira's lantern. She's had it a long time.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: She looks after it. Yours is ready to take home, if that's
where you're going.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Did the handle stay where we put it?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: It did. I've secured it and checked the joins.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can I carry it this time?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Try it. Keep it clear of the ground, and give yourself
room when you turn.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I'll mind the other side.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Would you like me to take the drawing?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Don't fold it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I can keep it flat in my satchel.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. Is this the paper for the sides?

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Yes. Try your design on a spare piece first. Leave the
covering loose until you're happy with it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I want the stairs to go round here.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Then lay the paper beside your drawing and see how
much room you have.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: The drawing's got quite a few steps.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I know how many.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: You can change your mind when you try them. That's
what the spare piece is for.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I'll take the loose sheets with the drawing.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Please don't put anything on top.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I won't.

pages.speaker: mira
lines: Ready, Liam? You can lift it now.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: There you are. Have you eaten anything since you left?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: We went to the mill.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: That doesn't answer me.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: (amused) He asked about buns.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: There weren't any there.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Then you've come to the right place for bread, at least.
Is that your lantern?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: The frame. We haven't put the paper on.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: I see. It's taller than I expected.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's a tower.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: So it is. Mind the corner as you come past.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Mira helped him make it. The drawing and paper are
with me.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Thank you, both of you. There's room to put them down
here.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can I leave the frame where Daisy won't knock it?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: On the table. Set it well back from the edge, and we'll
keep the food at this end.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Your mother's still at the school?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: She'll still be at the school. I'll hear all about the
afternoon when she's back.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Ada got paste on her sleeve.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Then perhaps I'll hear about that, too.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: She knew we might stop at some of the preparations.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Good. Have a break before you go anywhere else. You
look ready for one.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can you keep the paper flat?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes. Let's put everything down carefully.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: There. Bread and something to drink. You two help
yourselves as well.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Thank you.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I will. Thank you.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: The wheel was really loud.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: At the mill?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: You could hear it before we got there. Halden showed us
where to stand.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Did you stay there?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. The water doesn't go in the flour.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: That's good to hear.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: He wanted to know what it could grind.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I wasn't going to put anything in.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: He asked first. Halden was happy to let us look.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Then I'm glad you went. Finish that bite before you tell
me the rest.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: There is more.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: I thought there might be.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: There's more bread if you'd like it, Tomas.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Yes, please.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: You already had some.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: So did you.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: (grinning) I don't think we've finished.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Help yourselves. Yours goes on the table when you're
done, Liam.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: There's time to sit a little longer, Liam.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I want to try the paper now. My feet don't have to do
anything for that.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It fitted before.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: On the drawing?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. This bit's too small.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Show me where you want the last step.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: There. But then there's no room for the window.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Could the stairs turn sooner?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: They're meant to go all the way round.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Would another piece underneath help you try it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Don't draw it for me.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I won't. Show me where to hold it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: This corner. It's moving when I rub that bit.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: You can use a fresh piece. There's no need to rub
through this one.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: But I got the top right.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Keep it beside you, then. You can look at the top while
you try the stairs again.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: (frustrated) I know what I want it to look like.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I know. The drawing helped Mira see it, didn't it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Could you try a few bigger steps on this piece? Just to
see.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: There wouldn't be as many.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: You'd have room for the window.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Maybe. Can I keep the other piece, too?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Of course. I'll keep the food away from it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I'm holding this corner. Tell me when you want to move
it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. Don't let go yet.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: (quietly) I thought Elira would be glad not to carry it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Her lantern?

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Yes. I thought I was helping.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: She was glad you asked.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: But she still wanted to carry it herself.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I didn't think about that.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: She told you. You said all right.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I nearly tried to persuade her.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I'm glad you didn't.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: So am I. I can mind the door.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: She'll be expecting you now.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I'll be there.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I wasn't sure what to say when she went quiet.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: You offered to stay.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I wanted to.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I'm glad we did.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Caelan? Can you look at this bit?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Coming. How are the stairs?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: There's room for the window now. I haven't decided
about the bottom.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Why does Elira take the lantern for her husband?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: To remember him when everyone gathers.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: She already remembers him.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: She does. Taking it lets her do that with other people.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Is that why it's called Returning Light?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We believe the life in us returns to the gods when we
die. The festival is part of how we remember that.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: What comes back?

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: The life. That's what Caelan means by returning.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: But Elira still wanted him here.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes. You heard how much she misses him.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I liked when she was laughing.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: So did I.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can we ask Serene about it?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Of course. She'll give you time to ask.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: If you're going up to the sanctuary, leave the frame here.
I'll keep it safe.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: And the drawing. I want to use that piece again.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: All of it stays together on the table.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Would you like some more to drink before we go?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: No, thank you. I'm ready.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Thank you for the bread.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: You're welcome. Stay together, you three.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: We will. Don't let Daisy have the paper.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: I'll keep an eye on it. Go and have your talk.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Hello, you three. Have you come to show me the lantern?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's at home. The frame's finished, but the paper isn't.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Then I shall look forward to seeing it when you're ready.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Liam had some questions after our visit to Elira.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Did you enjoy seeing her?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. She told us how her husband got the song wrong.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Every year, apparently.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: (smiling) That sounds like a conversation worth having.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Am I keeping you from that?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: These papers can wait a little. Tell me what you wanted
to ask.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Caelan said the life goes back to the gods.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Yes. That's what we believe.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I don't think I understood it.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: All right. We can take our time.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We're not in a hurry.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We've had something to eat, too.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Good. Then we'll be comfortable.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: What part of Elira's husband comes back?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: We speak of the life that was in him. The life in all of us.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Like the life in me?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Yes. We believe it returns to the gods when we die.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Does any of it go inside the lantern?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: No, love. It's still a lamp. Elira carries it to remember her
husband.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Why does she light it, then?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: It gives her something to carry when we gather. She can
stand with the people who remember him, and with
people who want to keep her company.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Even if they didn't know him?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Yes. You hadn't heard him sing, had you?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: No. I wanted to.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: You listened when she told you about him.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: He put a garden gate in it.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: And sang it louder when she tried to tell him.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: (laughing softly) Poor Elira. I can imagine her face.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: She laughed, too. And then she got quiet.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: You can remember something funny and wish the
person were here to laugh with you.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Does she still believe what you said? About the gods?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: I believe she does.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: But she still wants him here.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Of course. She misses sharing her days with him. Her
faith doesn't stop her missing that.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Is the whole festival for people who've died?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Remembering them is part of it. So is being here
together.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Like taking bread to the Venns?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Yes. They're still part of the celebration if they spend the
evening at home.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Their mother said she'd speak to you when they know
what they can manage.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Then we'll wait to hear from her. I'm glad you visited.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: They've been choosing colors for a decoration.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yellow at both ends. Their mum's doing the ties.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: That sounds lovely.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: What if someone doesn't want to sing?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: They can listen. You don't have to do every part of the
evening.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Elira said some people just listen.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: She was right.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I was mostly thinking about the food before.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Are you still looking forward to it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: So am I.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I want to hear Elira sing. She said we could find her.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Then I think she'll be glad to see you.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Was there something else you wanted to ask?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I don't think so. Not yet.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: You can ask another time if you think of something.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I thought Elira might not want to come if it made her
sad.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: She can decide what she wants to do. We can make sure
she's welcome when she comes.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I'm going to mind her door when she brings the lantern
out.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Good. That sounds useful.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Thank you for giving us the time.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: I'm glad you brought him. How did the work at Mira's go?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's still a tower. We had to change the roof a bit.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: And leave somewhere for the heat to go.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I know about that now. The stairs are the hard part.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Are they coming along?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I've tried them on a spare piece. There's room for the
window.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Then you've made some progress today.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: (pleased) I tied one of the corners myself.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: You'll have to show me when it's finished.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I will. And Elira. And Mum hasn't seen it yet.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: It's safe at home. We can think about the rest when
you're ready.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. Thank you, Serene.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: You're very welcome, Liam.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can we go and finish it now?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Your lantern?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mum hasn't seen the frame yet. I want the paper on
when I show her.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: It's all waiting at home.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: Then I shall let you get back to it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Will you still be here later?

pages.speaker: serene
lines: For a while. If you've more to ask, you know where to
find me.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I want to show you the stairs when they're done.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: I'd like that.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Thank you again.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: You're welcome. Enjoy the rest of your afternoon.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Come on, then. Your father will be wondering how we
got on.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I'll tell him. I remember what she said.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: All right. We'll walk back together.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We've got time. We're staying together.

pages.speaker: serene
lines: I'll be here with my papers for a while. Enjoy your
afternoon together.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Back again. Was Serene able to give you some time?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: She was. Thank you for keeping everything here.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: It's just where you left it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Daisy didn't get the paper?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: No. Your drawing's still beside it, too.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Good. I want this piece.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: The one with the bigger steps?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. There's room for the window on that one.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Then make yourselves comfortable. Shall we clear a little
space for the work?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We can keep the practice pieces together at this end.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Don't throw the first one away.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: I won't.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: You can keep all of them. We only need room for the
piece you're using.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: And the frame.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I know. I haven't forgotten how big it is.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Let's look at the drawing again.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Caelan?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Elira carries one for her husband.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: What about someone who hasn't got anybody there?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: At the gathering?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Nobody to carry theirs.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Were you thinking of someone?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I don't know anyone like that. But there might be.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Were you thinking of carrying yours for them?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Could I?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: If that's what you'd like.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Even if I don't know their name?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Yes.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: (after a moment) I think I would.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: All right.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It can still be a tower?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Of course.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Good. I want to keep the window.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: These are the steps you tried before.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Those ones fit. The little ones went too far round.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Would you like me to hold this corner?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. Don't move it yet.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Tell me when.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Which of these sheets is the final piece?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: This one. I'm keeping that one to look at.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Then keep the two apart while you work. I'll help with the
fastening afterward.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Where do you want the first step?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Here. Then it turns before the window.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: You could mark the turn first.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I want to start at the bottom.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: All right. I'll hold this side.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Not on the line.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: Here?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. That's better.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Is my corner still where you want it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It is. Wait until I've checked the top.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Take your time. The frame isn't going anywhere.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. I know where I want it now.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Before we fasten it, we'll try the paper around the frame.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: With the window facing out?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Yes. You show me which side you want at the front.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: This one. That's where the stairs come round.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Would you like me to steady the frame?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes, please.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I can keep the loose edge from curling.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Good. Liam, hold the paper lightly while we line it up.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Will it cover the point?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: The point stays. We keep the opening at the top clear,
just as Mira showed you.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I remember.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Ready at this side.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Then let's fit it and see where the edges meet.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Don't fasten it until I've looked at the window.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: We won't.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I can see the window.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: And the turn in the stairs.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: The edges meet here. Are you happy with where they
are?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can this one go a little further?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: A little. Keep the bottom level.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Show me where you'd like it held.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Here. Until Dad fastens that part.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: All right.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: I'll do the small fastening. You can hold the edge for me.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Like this?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Yes. Keep your fingers there.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: What about the other side?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: We'll go around it a little at a time. No need to pull it all
tight at once.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I don't want the window bent.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Then we'll keep checking it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We're ready, Liam.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. Let's do it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: It's got all the sides on.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: It has. Let me check the joins and the handle before you
pick it up.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: It looks like your tower.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: That step bends.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: A little.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I could do it again.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Would you like to?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: (looking at it) No. I like the window.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: The covering is secure. The opening's clear, and Mira's
handle is holding well.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can I turn it?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Gently. Give yourself room, like you did with the frame.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I'll stand back.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mum will see it straight away, won't she?

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: She saw the drawing. You can show her how you made it
fit.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I want to tell her about the knot, too.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: You can tell her all of it. She's still at the school.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I'm carrying it myself.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We know. We're coming with you.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Ready? Lift it carefully and see how it feels.

pages.speaker: tessa
lines: Did you finish it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. It's got the window now.

pages.speaker: tessa
lines: It really is a tower.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I said it was going to be.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Liam? There you are.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mum, look.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Just a moment, love. Tessa, leave that piece flat while it
dries. Thank you.

pages.speaker: tessa
lines: All right.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Now, let me see. You've been busy.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mira helped with the frame. Then we finished it at home.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: His father helped us with the covering.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Thank you for bringing him back. Is he going to let me
have a proper look?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. But I'm holding it.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Of course you are. Come where I can see the front.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Show me the stairs.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I had to use bigger ones. Otherwise there wasn't room
for the window.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: I see. They go around this side?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. That one's a bit bent.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: May I look closer?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Gently.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Of course. And this is the corner you tied?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Mira checked it afterward.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Then you've had good company while you made it.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: He did quite a lot himself.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Caelan held the paper where I wanted it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: He told us where.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: (smiling) I'm glad you worked it out together.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Do you like the point?

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: I do. It looks like the tower you showed me.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: We changed the roof a bit. There has to be room for the
heat.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Then I'm glad you listened to Mira.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: And who will you carry it for?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Someone who hasn't got one.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Someone without anybody there to carry a light for
them?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. Is that all right?

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Yes, love. We'll make room for it beside ours.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I'll keep hold of it.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Will you walk with me tomorrow?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I want to carry it myself.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: You can.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: I've still got some things to put away here.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Can I leave it with you?

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: There's rather a lot of paper about. I'd like yours kept
safely at home until tomorrow.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Dad said he would look after it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: We can walk him back and help him put it away.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: Thank you. I'll be home when we're finished here.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We won't keep him out this time.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: We've already shown you.

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: You have. And I'm glad you came.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Will you remember which side has the window?

pages.speaker: liam_mother
lines: I think I'll remember. You can show me again tomorrow.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. Come on, then.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: Together, Liam.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I know.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Did she get to see it?

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Yes. She liked the point.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: I thought she might.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: He showed her how the stairs fit, too.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: And the corner I tied.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Good. Now let's find it a safe place for the night.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: On the table?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Yes. I'll keep this space clear until tomorrow.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: The drawing and practice pieces can stay together at the
other side.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Daisy won't reach it there?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: It's well back from the edge. I'll mind it.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: All right. Which way should the window face?

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Where you can see it when you come in.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: This way, then. I'll set it down.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: There. You can see the window.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Yes. It's safe there.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Don't put anything on it.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: I won't.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You can look at it again before you leave tomorrow.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: I will. I want to see Elira's as well.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: She said to come and find her.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: And Serene hasn't seen this one yet.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You'll have time to show them.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Thank you for giving him the afternoon, both of you.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: I enjoyed it.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: So did I.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: Thank you for helping with the paper.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: You're welcome, Liam.

pages.speaker: tomas
lines: We'll see you tomorrow.

pages.speaker: liam
lines: At the lights.

pages.speaker: caelan
lines: At the lights.

pages.speaker: liam_father
lines: Go and get on with your preparations. We'll see you
there.
